I close my eyes on the patient man's town as the patient man's creature, and I start counting too — his weaknesses, his tree, his buried house, the day I find that surviving Sunn — because the leash goes both ways now, Corran, and I've got nothing but time to prove it.

Dawn comes up grey over the chains the way it came up on your first morning, and you are still here to see it, which is the only line of the ledger that never lies. You take the rest of the tally honest, the way you'd count a night's take: a little healed and a little bled; a leash turned to a weapon and a room saved with it; your people kept off his hook and the read that would've put your hand on his throat lost to a cold hundred years; and the one true rule of the string learned in full — that you can serve a patient man forever and never buy back an ounce of his patience. So you stop trying to win it in a night, because a woman who tries to is a woman who ends in the glass. You find a safe dry cot at last, the night's wolves all spent, and you lie down east with the counting dead and the sleeping living, and you let yourself have, finally, the whole of the rest you've chased since yesterday's dawn. Not hiding. Banking. A knife does not have to be drawn to be a knife. And as sleep takes you — the real kind, the knitting kind, the first full measure of it since before the flood — you begin, behind your closed eyes, to do the patient man's own arithmetic back at him: his weaknesses, his tree, his buried house, the surviving Sunn somewhere above the color, the day the leash learns it goes both ways. You close your eyes on the patient man's town as the patient man's creature, and you start counting too.
dmlog.dmNotes: T10a (close, first beat): she chooses the long game and lies down for the full rest denied all set. Applying rest{long} FIRST (T2 lesson) to read the actual heal + rest-risk before authoring the waking half.

dmlog.text:
You wake whole. It is such a strange thing after the night you've had that for a moment you don't trust it — but the shoulder holds, the ache is a memory, the blood is all back where blood belongs; the first full measure of rest since before the flood has knit you into a woman again, and Day Five finds you, for once, at your strength. And because you lay east again with the counting town, the Shared Sleep paid you the way it pays the ones who keep its courtesy: not a punishment, an omen. What the Traitor's Tree would not give your hands in the cold, the glass gave your sleeping eyes — not the whole of it, not the founding crime laid bare, but a direction, sure as a compass needle: the counting in the color runs one way, upriver, toward a house not all the way buried, and the surviving Sunn is no longer an inference you built from a short count — it is a certainty you dreamed from the site's own past. You don't have the lever yet. You have the bearing to it, and the cold sense that the dream spent something to give you the seeing — that the next time you'd have reached for luck, it will not be there. A fair price. Omens always cost.

So the day begins, and the ledger of the last one closes: Sella Voss, drowned in the flood, walks into her first full morning as the Ironwood Circle's own quiet creature — leashed and watched, healed and whole, her network safe behind a corpse that is her own faked death, her secrets all still folded small and warm where a patient man can't feel them. She lost the war she was always going to lose. But she is standing in the Day-Five dawn with her strength back and a bearing in her chest toward the one thing that could unmake the man who owns her, and all the time in the world to walk it. You said it at the Tree, Corran: the Maw is small. You'll work the sum of me. So will I. Only now I know which way your buried house lies — and you don't know I'm counting.

payload.what: By the dawn of Day Five, Sella Voss — the flood's 'drowned hero' — had survived her first full day as the Ironwood Circle's leashed asset: she protected the Refugee-Quarter network from her own owner's hunt behind a decoy built of her own faked death, but drew Corran Vale's fixed, patient interest onto herself, and set herself to work the sum of him from inside.

dm.setCloseState: T10-set4 CLOSE (Day 5 dawn): Sella ends her first full day as Corran's leashed mole HEALED (long rest finally uninterrupted → 9/9) and EQUILIBRIUM-SHIFTED. Ledger of the day: T3 weaponized the leash (bluffed wreckers off a room, saved sleepers); T5 pre-empted the two-legends danger; T6 tried a dead-culprit decoy to close Corran's network-hunt and FAILED (Deception 7 vs 16) → Corran now INTERESTED in her (undissolved); T7 severed the body-thread (glass eats its dead — unfalsifiable alibi); T8 read the Traitor's Tree for the Circle's founding crime and FAILED (Investigation 6 vs 15) — lever withheld; T9 damage-control rebuilt surface cover (true wrecker-intel) but did NOT buy off the interest. NET: she is now a SUSPECTED asset (Corran watching), but her network is safe, her 4 secrets (Ossle's killing, network membership, Maddan's Iron-Strap secret, the unspent ace) all still hidden, and she holds a NEW soft lead. Corran does NOT know she is the hero he closed the book on. The mole is planted, watched, and playing the long game he named.

dm.sunnBearing: T10-set4 CLOSE: the Shared Sleep taboo (obeyed east-facing) paid a 'Vivid Omens' rest-boon — a dream of the SITE'S PAST that gives Sella a soft DIRECTION toward the surviving Sunn heir: the counting in the glass runs upriver toward 'a house not all the way buried.' NOT the hard founding-crime canon (the T8 tree-read FAILED to earn that) — an Insight/bearing only, a lead to pull next set. Cost (engine 'lose your next Boon'): her next luck/boon is spent. The Sunn-heir thread is now a live compass for Sella, still unconfirmed as hard canon. Also pending (engine 'Camp cooking' risk): a creature will try to steal food at her next rest (trivial flavor, delayed).

dmlog.dmNotes: T10b (close, resolution beat): she wakes full (9/9) and the 'Vivid Omens' rest-risk is honored as an INSIGHT/bearing toward the surviving Sunn — deliberately NOT the hard founding-crime canon the T8 tree-fail withheld (no consolation-canon; a lead, not the lever), with its 'lose next Boon' cost recorded. fact_canonized closes the set's durable equilibrium (+1 XP legit, resolves to text). No roll (a settled close beat + engine-granted rest omen). The set lands her tenser and richer than it opened: healed, watched, network-safe, secrets intact, a new compass — the long game engaged. Bookends the set's rest-plagued open.

dmlog.text: Whole at last, and for the first time in five days nobody's hunting me this exact minute — so I use it, because a patient man's patience is the one thing I can borrow against. But I don't go charging upriver after a dream; a leashed woman who bolts for the town line is a woman who's just told her owner where to point. First I turn the bearing into a name. So I go quiet and careful back to the fen-wife who mended me — one old woman, not the whole network, and a woman who already knows both my faces and kept her mouth shut anyway. I take the long way, doubling my path twice and watching the slower faces for the one that turns when I turn, because if Corran's put eyes on me I'd rather feed them a boring morning than a Sunn. When I'm sure of my back I sit down with her low and warm and I ask her the old question the young ones can't answer: before the Circle, before the chains hung heavy — the Sunns who kept the Throat, the house that went into the glass. Did all of them go down? Or is there a room upriver that still remembers its own name.

When I'm sure of my back I sit down with her low and warm and I ask her the old question the young ones can't answer: before the Circle, before the chains hung heavy — the Sunns who kept the Throat, the house that went into the glass. Did all of them go down? Or is there a room upriver that still remembers its own name.

The fen-wife does not answer at once. She looks at the doorway you came through, and the one you didn't, the way a woman checks a pot for a crack before she trusts it with water — and only when she's satisfied your back is your own does she let the old thing up out of her.

"Went down," she says, testing the words like a sore tooth. "That's the Circle's grammar, girl. Houses don't go down. They get put down, slow, a name at a time, so no one morning ever looks like the murder it is." Her hands keep working out of habit, folding a strip of linen that doesn't need folding. "The Sunns kept the Throat before there was a Circle to keep anything. The well was theirs — the burning water, the whole wound of it. And a house that owns the one thing everybody needs is a house the patient ones have all the time in the world to unwrite. Haldrek. Wemric. You'll have seen those two lately, I think, by the look you came in with. They were only the last of the crossings-out. It's been a hundred years of them."

She stops folding. This is the part she has to decide to say, and you watch her decide it. "There was a girl they got out. Before the end of it — smuggled up past the Leat when she was small enough to be somebody's niece instead of somebody's heir. If she lived, she's up where the river bends and the old well-house sits half-sunk in the glass — not all the way buried, they say, which in this town is the most dangerous thing a thing can be." Her eyes come up to yours, flat and frightened and kind all at once. "They called her **Wren**. It's not her name. Her name is the thing the Circle's spent a hundred years making sure dies quiet." A beat. "And you, wearing the good coat, asking after Sunns — girl, that's not a question you ask twice. A patient man will let a lot ripen. Not that. Ask after Wren where the wrong ear hears it, and you'll find out how fast the patient ones can move when the well's what's on the table."

fields.role: the last Sunn heir (child-nickname; true name suppressed)

dm.lead: The surviving Sunn heir, got out as a small girl before the house was finished off; hidden upriver where the river bends, at the old Sunn well-house 'half-sunk in the glass, not all the way buried' (aligns with the T10-set4 Vivid-Omens dream-bearing + the Miller's-Leat upriver geography). The living claimant to the Throat's well = the one lever on the Circle's whole power. UNMET; a lead only. True name still suppressed (the deepest gate). Named to Sella by the fen-wife (network elder, referred-by-role, unminted) on Day 5, Refugee Quarter.
dm.danger: The fen-wife's explicit warning: asking after the Sunns is the ONE question that turns Corran's patient interest to iron — the Circle exists to keep that name dead, and it will move FAST if the well is on the table. Compounds Sella's already-live suspected-asset exposure.

dm.sunnLeadGiven: T1-set09: the fen-wife (who mended Sella, knows both her faces) converted Sella's soft dream-bearing into a concrete lead — confirmed the Sunns kept the Throat's well before the Circle and have been 'put down a name at a time' over a hundred years (Haldrek/Wemric only the latest), and named a surviving heir: a girl smuggled out young, 'Wren' (child-nickname, true name suppressed), living upriver at the half-sunk Sunn well-house past the Leat. No roll (willing trusted elder). She WITHHELD/does-not-hold the deepest part — WHO worked the founding betrayal (still gated at the Tree; DM-truth: Maddan). She warned asking after Sunns hardens Corran fast.

dmlog.dmNotes: Willing trusted elder → no persuasion gamble; the drip converts the dream-bearing into a pursuable lead (Wren, upriver well-house) while gating the founding-traitor identity (the Tree secret, unread T8) and planting the exact danger (Sunn-questions harden Corran). Minted Wren as a soft lead so the thread survives to the next DM.

dmlog.text: A woman who can't go where she wants goes there on her owner's leash instead — the trick isn't slipping the string, it's making the string want to reach the same place I do. So I find Fenn on the spans and I give him a report shaped like initiative, the diligent-asset voice Corran's been testing me in. "The wrecker crew I flagged didn't come up out of nowhere," I tell him. "Organized men work from a nest, and everything the flood spat into those upper rooms came down FROM upriver — the Leat, the water feeding the Throat, the whole approach nobody's walked since the gauge broke ten-year. Corran wants his count clean? His count's got a whole upriver flank he's blind on, and I'm the one set of eyes he's already got broken in for exactly this. Let me walk it — the bend, the old channels, the flood-source — and I'll bring back what loosened up there and where the wreckers den. A day, maybe two." I say nothing at all about a girl or a well-house or a house not all the way buried. I let him hear a creature volunteering to be useful in the one direction I mean to go anyway, and I keep my face the face of a woman who's only ever thinking about his problems.

Fenn hears you out on the swaying span, the noon glare coming up hard off the glass below, and he does what Fenn does: he takes the whole of it at exact change, no more face than a ledger shows. "Upriver," he repeats, as if setting the word down somewhere to be weighed later. "A day. Maybe two." He doesn't say yes. He doesn't say no. He folds himself back toward the ironwood door with your initiative in his pocket, and you're left to stand in the white light and understand that you have just asked a patient, already-curious man to let his newest, half-trusted eyes walk out of his sight toward the one edge of the map he can't watch — and that everything now rides on whether the pretext you built reads, to the best reader in the Maw, as a diligent creature volunteering for a blind spot, or as a leashed woman who wants very badly to be somewhere upriver for reasons of her own. The line goes out. You wait to feel what comes back on it.
dmlog.dmNotes: Fair moderate Deception gamble (DC15, no adv): strong true-brick pretext vs a suspicious reader. Success = leash-as-road (sanctioned passage, no escort). NearMiss = passage WITH a Circle watcher bolted on (Ledd). Fail = denied + Corran sends his own man upriver, turning his eye toward the bend (the exact thing Sella swore not to do). No front tick on any branch (an errand granted/denied is not a faction move).

dmlog.text: The line comes back slack and easy. Fenn returns before the glare has moved far: "He says: walk it. Two days. Bring him the wreckers' den and whatever the flood loosened, and mind you come back — a set of eyes that wanders off is just a thing he has to replace." No escort named, no shadow set that you can find. He has read a useful creature volunteering for a real hole in his count, and he has handed you, without knowing it, the one road you wanted: sanctioned passage upriver, wearing his errand like a coat. Any eyes that clock you making for the bend will read the Circle's own business, not a Sunn. You have turned the leash into a road.

dm.grantedUpriver: T2-set09 (Deception success): Corran bought Sella's diligent-asset pretext and sanctioned a 2-day upriver errand (find the wrecker den + flood-loosened intel), no escort named/found. He reads a useful creature filling a real blind spot in his count — he does NOT know the true target is Wren / the surviving Sunn / the well-house upriver. Sella now has COVER to move toward the bend: the leash turned into a road. Deadline: 2 days, come back or be 'a thing he has to replace.'

dmlog.text: I go upriver the way I do everything now — wearing the errand honestly, because a true report is the only kind that survives Corran, and because the errand and my own hunt run the same road anyway. So I actually work it: I read the flood-scars along the Leat, mark where the old channels blew out and where the water came from, and I keep my eye peeled for the wrecker sign — a beached boat, a cache, a trampled bank, anything I can carry back down the string as the diligent thing I promised. But every step of the honest errand carries me toward the bend, and I let it, unhurried, one more Circle creature walking her owner's flank. As the light goes long I come up on where the river turns and the glass shallows out, watching for the thing the fen-wife named — a well-house half-sunk in the color, not all the way buried — and reading the ground around it before I go a foot closer, because a house that's outlived a hundred years of crossings-out didn't do it by being easy to walk up on.

The Maw thins behind you as the chains give way to bank and reed, and the errand pays out honest coin the way you hoped: a mile up the Leat you find where the flood was born — an old sluice-gate rotted through and never mended, the channel behind it silted to uselessness, so the river had nowhere to go but over the town. That alone is worth the walk to Corran; a count-keeper likes to know his disaster had an address. And half a mile on you find the wreckers' sign — a flat-bottomed scavenger boat drawn up under a cut bank, a cache of pried fittings and waterlogged goods under oiled canvas, cold ashes, no men. A den, empty in daylight, exactly where an organized crew would keep it. You mark it all, the diligent creature's true harvest, and you carry it toward the bend.

And then the river turns, and there it is. The glass runs shallow here, gone from wound-color to a milky green like old ice, and rising up out of it — canted, one whole corner drunk-deep in the fused ground — stands a squat stone **well-house**, older than the chains, its roof-ridge still sharp against the failing light. Not all the way buried. The fen-wife's exact words, and there they are in stone. But you did not outlive a hundred years by walking up to lit windows, and you don't now — you stop in the reeds and read it, and the ground reads back. There is a thread of smoke, thin and smokeless-careful, the fire of someone who does not want a fire seen. There is a line of pale cord strung ankle-high across the only dry approach, set by a hand that expects company it won't like. And every shutter on the canted house faces east — squared to the crater, the way the drowned lie, the way the whole Maw sleeps — except one, on the near side, cracked a finger's width and dark, and angled at you. Something in that house is already awake, already facing the wrong way on purpose, and already watching the reeds you're standing in.

dm.located: T3-set09: Sella reached the bend upriver and SIGHTED the well-house the fen-wife named — a squat pre-Circle stone well-house canted into milky shallow glass ('not all the way buried', exact). Telegraphed as OCCUPIED and WARY, not empty: a careful smokeless fire, a tripline of pale cord across the only dry approach, and every shutter squared east (Shared-Sleep taboo) EXCEPT one near-side shutter cracked and angled at the reeds — something inside is awake, facing the wrong way on purpose, and already watching her. She has NOT approached yet. This is Wren (or Wren's keeper); an old survivor does not welcome company.
dm.errandCover: En route Sella gathered TRUE errand-intel for Corran (survives a patient reader): the flood's source = a rotted unmended upriver sluice-gate + silted channel; the wrecker den = a beached scavenger boat + goods-cache under a cut bank, empty in daylight. Her cover-deliverable is real.

dmlog.dmNotes: Travel beat = no gratuitous roll (her real gambles come at the approach/meeting where her strong skills apply). Delivered true errand-intel so her cover survives Corran; made the well-house a node; planted the meeting as hard-and-dangerous — telegraphed the house is occupied + wary + already watching (tripline, careful fire, the one east-broken shutter). Poised into T4's approach.

dmlog.text: A body that's already watching me is a body I do not sneak up on — sneaking's what the last hundred years of killers did, and this house is still standing because it knows that walk. So I do the opposite. I step out of the reeds into the last of the light where the broken shutter can see me whole, and I stop dead at the pale cord, deliberate, and I look down at it and then up at the dark gap so whoever's behind it knows I saw the trap and chose not to cross it. I open both hands, empty, out from my sides. And I give the truth first, because truth is the only key that fits a lock this old — pitched low and steady, no closer. "I know whose house this is. I know they called the girl Wren, and I know that's not her name, and I know why it isn't." A breath. "I'm wearing the wrong coat. I know it. I wear it because the same patient man who's spent a hundred years crossing your family off a list keeps me on a string too — and I got tired of being on it. Haldrek. Wemric. Struck out on his own slate not a week gone. I'm not here to finish the count. I'm here because a house that's not all the way buried is the one thing in the whole Maw that scares Corran Vale — and I would very much like to scare him." I don't move. I let the cord stay uncrossed between us, and I wait to be believed or shot.

For a long moment the only answer is the river and the tick of cooling glass, and the dark gap in the shutter does not change at all — which is its own answer, because a frightened person slams a shutter and a dangerous one holds it still. Then, without the shutter moving, a sound: the small dry double-click of a crossbow's catch being thumbed off, unhurried, from somewhere the angle of the wall says is NOT behind that shutter at all — she moved while you were talking, and the broken shutter was the decoy, and you have been reciting your pretty truths at an empty window. The voice comes from your right, low and level and much closer than it should be, a young woman's voice with a hundred years of caution filed into it: "Everyone who ever came to kill my family knew all the right names too." A pause, the bolt steady on you across the reeds. "You've got the length of my patience to tell me why a Circle coat that knows my dead should walk away from this bend still breathing. And I warn you — I've heard every lie the good coats tell. My whole life is the list of them." She does not step into the light. She waits, and everything now rests on whether the woman who outlived the crossings-out reads truth in you, or one more clever mouth sent up the river to finish what the slate started.
dmlog.dmNotes: Honest skill choice = Persuasion (she persuades with truth, not a sold lie), advantage for strong true levers offsetting no-proficiency, DC15 vs a hostile-by-history survivor. The setup pays off the telegraph — she moved during the speech, the broken shutter was a decoy (rewards the player's read that a survivor is trap-smart). Success = wary provisional alliance INSIDE, knife's-edge. NearMiss = standoff, trust priced at a hostage-truth (forces Sella to spend a secret). Fail = spooked + fled + warned (the lead goes to ground). No front tick (a private meeting).

dmlog.text: The bolt does not lower, but the silence changes weight — she is listening now, not just aiming. "A Circle string that got tired of being on it," she repeats, tasting it for the rot, and finding, to her own visible anger, none. She steps out of the dark at last: a young woman, lean and river-weathered, older in the eyes than the rest of her, the crossbow still up but no longer pointed at the middle of you. "Wren," she says, giving you the child-name like a coin she despises. "Since you already spent it." She looks at the cord you didn't cross, and at the coat you disowned, and something in her makes a hard, cold decision to gamble on you because a hundred years of hiding has bought her family exactly nothing. "You want to scare Corran Vale. Coat." A thin, humorless breath. "Come in off the cold, then, before his next-best hunter reads the same reeds you did. But you cross that threshold knowing: everyone who's ever learned where I sleep is dead. You'll be the first exception or the next entry."

dm.met: T4-set09 (Persuasion success, adv): FIRST CONTACT. Wren = a young river-weathered woman, the last Sunn, hunted her whole life, crossbow-competent and trap-smart (she moved during Sella's speech; the broken shutter was a decoy). Sella disarmed the good-coat threat by leading with TRUTH (saw+respected the tripline, named the struck dead Haldrek/Wemric, disowned the coat, offered the shared enemy Corran + the honest aim 'I want to scare him'). Wren made a hard cold decision to gamble on Sella out of a century of futile hiding — let her INSIDE, wary, crossbow still handy, on an explicit knife's-edge ('the first exception or the next entry'). NOT trust yet; a provisional alliance of shared enemy. True name still suppressed even to Sella.

dmlog.text: I step over the cord — not around it, over it, letting her see I trust her not to have set a second one under my foot — and I take the seat nearest her careful little fire, hands still where she can watch them. "You said the first exception or the next entry. Fair. So I'll go first, and I'll give you the knife myself." I say it plain, no charlatan's music in it for once. "The Circle thinks I'm dead. Not run off — dead. I drowned myself off their own books in the flood, struck my own name so a patient man would stop looking. The woman sitting at your fire doesn't exist; there's a grave in a ledger with my name in it. You breathe one word of that down the river and my whole life comes apart in a morning — so now we each hold the other's throat, and maybe that's the only kind of trust two dead women get." I let that sit. Then, low: "Two things, and then I'll earn the rest. One — the founding. Not the crossings-out you lived; the FIRST one. How did the Circle ever come to own a well that was your family's? Because whatever really happened, they buried it under a tree and killed a hundred years of people to keep it buried. Two —" and here I actually want the answer, not just the intel "— what do you want, Wren? Not what I want to scare him with. You. A house not all the way buried wants something, or it lies all the way down. What's kept you breathing up here alone?"

Wren watches you step over the cord instead of around it, and something in her jaw unclenches by a degree — not trust, but its first cousin, the respect of one careful animal for another. She sets the crossbow down at last, though within reach, and when you give her the grave-in-a-ledger she does not gloat at holding your throat. She just nods, slow, like a woman recognizing her own reflection in bad light. "Two dead women," she says. "Aye. It's the only trust our kind gets — the mutual kind, with a drop under both our feet." She feeds a splinter to the careful fire. "I'll keep your grave if you keep mine."

Then the founding, and here her voice goes to the flat place people keep their oldest wounds. "I was small. So what I've got is a child's size of it, and a child's certainty it's true. The well was ours — the Throat, the burning water, back when it was a gift and not a leash. And one night it wasn't ours anymore, and the reason it stopped being ours was that someone opened the door. Not a siege. Not a war. A door, from the inside, by a hand that ate at our table. The Circle didn't take the Throat, coat. Somebody GAVE it to them, and then the tree got planted over the giving so no one could ever dig up whose hand it was." Her eyes are hard and wet at once. "I don't know the name. That's the thing they killed my whole house to keep me from knowing — and it's the thing that'd end them, because a well got by a traitor's gift is a well the whole Maw would take back if they knew. Steal a thing and it's yours by strength. Be GIVEN it by treachery and it's yours by a lie — and lies can be made loud."

She looks at you then, the last Sunn, and answers your second question with the smallest, fiercest want you've heard in this whole grim town. "You asked what I want. Not the well. I can't drink a well. I want the name." A breath. "The real one. Mine — the one they made die quiet — said ONCE, out loud, somewhere it can't be un-said, so that my father and his father and all of them under the glass were PEOPLE and not just marks a patient man crossed off. Make the quiet loud, coat. That's all I've got left to want." And, quieter, a strategist under the grief: "There's them that'd help you do it, if you're mad enough. The Circle's got one true enemy in the Maw — the **Navigator's Lodge**. They and the Circle have been at each other's throats for years. A Lodge that got handed proof the Circle's whole claim is a traitor's gift? They'd drag it into the light and never stop. But Lodge folk are no gentler than Circle folk, girl. You'd be handing my name to another set of hands that wants it for their war, not for me."

dm.exchange: T5-set09: Sella bought real trust by spending collateral — told Wren she's the 'drowned hero' who struck her OWN name off the Circle's books (faked death). Two-dead-women mutual-hostage trust struck ('I'll keep your grave if you keep mine'). Wren reciprocated with the SUNN side of the founding: the Throat/well was the Sunns'; it was LOST because someone OPENED THE DOOR FROM THE INSIDE — a betrayal by a hand 'that ate at our table', then the Traitor's Tree was planted over it to bury WHOSE hand. Wren does NOT know the traitor's name (killed-to-keep-her-from-it as a child) — the gate HELD (DM-truth: Maddan). The lever's logic: a well got by treachery is 'yours by a lie, and lies can be made loud.'
dm.want: Wren's want is NOT the well/power/revenge — she wants her SUPPRESSED TRUE NAME said ONCE, publicly, un-un-sayable, so her erased family 'were people and not marks.' Aligns with the Circle-internal front + the Navigator's Lodge agenda (drag a buried truth into the light). Provisional ally, wary; still holds her hard proof close (not yet handed over).
dm.holdsProof: Wren implies she has/can-get PROOF the claim is a traitor's gift (not yet shown to Sella — guarded until there's a real plan). The physical lever stays a slow-drip.

dm.drownedSecretSpent: T5-set09: Sella deliberately SPENT one of her four intact secrets — she told Wren (a hunted stranger) that she's the 'drowned hero' who faked her own death off the Circle's books. New latent EXPOSURE: if Wren ever speaks it down the river, Sella's cover collapses in a morning. Traded knowingly as mutual-hostage collateral. (Sella's remaining unshared-from-Corran secrets: killed clerk Ossle; is network's; holds Maddan's Iron-Strap secret unspent.)

dm.surfacedAsLever: T5-set09: named by Wren as the Circle's one true enemy in the Maw (at open war). A living-Sunn traitor's-gift proof handed to the Lodge = they'd 'drag it into the light and never stop' (matches their agenda: bury or expose a dangerous truth). BUT Wren warns the Lodge is 'no gentler than Circle folk' — they'd want the Sunn name for their WAR, not for Wren. The long-untouched faction (0/6) now has a live hook into the Sella/Sunn arc. Unengaged; a potential ally-or-user, double-edged.

dmlog.dmNotes: Willing exchange bought with real collateral (Sella spends the drowned-hero secret) → no gamble roll. Delivered the founding SHAPE (a betrayal from inside, the tree planted over WHOSE hand) while gating the traitor's identity even from Wren (she was a child) — a shared unknown = the live Tree/Maddan quest. Wren's want (her true name made loud) gives the alliance a human aim and threads the Navigator's Lodge (untouched faction) as a double-edged path. The turn COSTS Sella a secret (mechanical/narrative honesty). Held Wren's hard proof close (slow drip).

dmlog.text: "Then we're agreed on the wanting," I say. "Your name, loud. And I'll tell you true, Wren — I came up here for a lever to hold on the man who owns me, and I'm not going to pretend that's changed. But a lever that gives you your dead back is a lever I can hold with a clean hand for once, so let's make it the same crowbar and both of us pull." I lean in, all business now, the planner in me awake. "Which means I need two things from you, and then we move — because I'm on a two-day string and you told me yourself his next hunter reads reeds as well as I do. First: the proof. You said a well got by a traitor's gift is a lie that can be made loud — so you've got something that PROVES the gift, or the shape of one, or you'd have said 'story,' not 'lie.' I need to see it, or know where it sleeps. Second: the WHERE. A name shouted in an empty reed-bed is just weather. If we take this to your Navigator's Lodge they make it their war and you a banner; if we take it to the wrong ear it dies with us. So where does a thing get shouted in the Maw so loud a patient man can't quiet it after?" And while she weighs it, I keep half an ear bent to the river behind me — because two days is Corran's mercy, not his patience, and I'd like to hear the boat before it hears us.

"Same crowbar," Wren says, and for the first time the ghost of something that isn't grief crosses her face. "I can pull with that." Then she answers your first question by looking down — straight down, through the canted floor, to where the milky glass glows faint under the boards. "You want the proof. It's not in a box, coat. My people weren't fools; a thing in a box is a thing that gets found and burned. They put it where only a Sunn would ever go to look." Her jaw tightens. "The well drops into the glass. And the glass keeps what it takes — you'll know that, if you've lived in the Maw a week. Down there, where the water goes to color, my grandfather sank the true deed of the Throat, and the roll of our own name, sealed in the burning-water resin that won't rot — under the counting dead, with the counting dead, because the drowned settle east and go on keeping the tally, and a Sunn is the only one who can lie down among them facing the right way and come back up. It's a taboo and a lock both. That's where it sleeps."

She lets that land, then answers your second, and her voice drops to the flat certainty of someone naming a gallows. "And there's only one place in the Maw a thing gets said so loud it can't be quieted. You've already been there. The tree. The Traitor's Tree is the Maw's own courthouse — has been since before the chains — the one spot where a thing spoken is witnessed by the whole town and binds. They planted it over the giving to bury my name." Her eyes come up, bright and terrible. "So we dig my name up out of the glass, and we say it loud at the very tree they buried it under, in front of the whole Maw, where a patient man can't un-say a word of it. Poetry, coat. The kind that gets people killed."

And that is exactly when the thing you'd bent half an ear for arrives. Not a sound — a light. Far down the black river where you came up, a single lantern rides the water, low and steady, coming against the current at the one pace that means it is not in any hurry at all. Unhurried. In the Maw that is not a comfort; it is a signature. Someone is coming up the river in the dark, taking all the time in the world, and the well-house at the bend is the only reason anyone rows this stretch after moonrise.

dm.proofLocation: T6-set09: Wren revealed WHERE the proof sleeps — NOT in a box (would be found+burned). Her grandfather sank the true DEED of the Throat + the roll of the Sunns' true name, sealed in rot-proof burning-water resin, DOWN THE WELL into the glass, 'under the counting dead, with the counting dead.' Only a Sunn can lie down among the drowned facing east (Shared Sleep taboo) and come back up — 'a taboo and a lock both.' (Payoff of the Sunn-in-glass thread: glass keeps its dead T7-set4 + the drowned count east + the dream-bearing.) Retrieving it = a dangerous descent into the glass — Wren (a Sunn) can go where Sella can't.
dm.plan: The plan sketched: retrieve the deed+name from the glass, then say Wren's true name LOUD at the Traitor's Tree — the Maw's courthouse, the one place a spoken thing is town-witnessed and binds, and the very tree planted over the burial. 'A patient man can't un-say a word of it.' High-stakes, on Corran's own ground.

dm.courthouseRole: T6-set09: established (via Wren) as the Maw's own COURTHOUSE since before the chains — the one place a thing spoken is witnessed by the whole town and BINDS (grounds the T8-set4 'bargaining-notch, the Maw's own courthouse' read). The Sunn plan's intended STAGE: dig the true name out of the glass and say it loud here, where Corran can't un-say it. The Tree the Circle planted to bury the founding becomes the pulpit to expose it.

dm.hunterInboundT6: T6-set09 TELEGRAPH: while planning, Sella (ear on the river) sees a single lantern coming UP the black river against the current at the unhurried pace that is a Circle signature (Corran's people never hurry — Day-1 canon). Someone is rowing the well-house stretch after moonrise — the only reason to row it is the bend/the well-house. Likely Corran's 'next-best hunter' (Wren's warning) or Corran's own man. Live inbound lethal threat; forces urgency on the glass-descent + the plan. Honest telegraph (danger always perceivable first).

dmlog.dmNotes: Willing planning exchange = no roll (the real check is banked for the glass-descent next turn). Paid off the Sunn-in-glass thread as the proof's LOCK (only a Sunn can retrieve it — a taboo-and-lock), and the Traitor's Tree as the intended STAGE (courthouse — the burial-lid becomes the pulpit). Ended on an honest lethal telegraph — an unhurried Circle-signature lantern coming up the river — to make the back half hard and time-pressured. No front tick (planning); the inbound is a telegraph, not yet an event.

dmlog.text: "That's a Circle boat," I tell her, already moving, already cold. "Nobody else rows this stretch to be nowhere. Which means we don't get two days after all — we get however long a slow man takes to reach a bend." I make the call fast, the way a con makes them. "Wren — go down. Now, while there's a reason for the house to be dark and empty. Get the deed and the name and don't come up for anything you hear up here; if it goes wrong the proof still lives and you still run, and that's a better night than both of us. Go." And then I do the one thing in this whole world I'm actually good at: I don't hide from the lantern, I walk DOWN to meet it, out onto the mud where the reeds thin, hands loose, and I become the diligent creature again — because I am, tonight, sanctioned, on the string, working this exact flank on Corran Vale's own word. I let them get a good look at a bored Circle asset who's already been up here half a day. "You're late, and you're loud," I call across the water, easy, before they can make me the surprise. "I've had the wrecker-den marked since noon and there's nothing else up this bend but silt and a rotted sluice-gate. Corran sent me to walk it. Who sent you — and does he know he's doubling the work on a flank I've already cleared?" I put the whole weight of the leash I hate into it, and I make his errand answer to mine.

Wren doesn't argue — a hundred years of hunting has taught her the sound of a plan that might work, and she's gone through a floor-hatch into the well's throat before your sentence is finished, swallowed by the faint milk-glow below. You walk the other way, out onto the cold mud where the reeds thin and the lantern-light can find you, and you make yourself into the most boring thing on the river: a Circle asset, bored, sanctioned, half a day into a dull errand. The boat resolves out of the dark — a single lean Circle man at the oars, no hurry in him, a whittling-knife of habit tucked at his belt and a face that has done this work a long time. He lets your challenge cross the water and doesn't answer it right away; he ships the oars, and lets the boat drift the last lengths in, and looks at you the way Corran looked at you the first morning — pricing, unbothered. "Voss," he says at last, so he was told a name before he came. "They did say you'd be up here." He does not say who they is, or whether the telling came with a warning. He sits in his drifting boat a few feet off the mud, your sanction and his errand hanging in the cold air between you, and waits to see whether the bored diligent creature is the whole of what he's looking at — while somewhere under your feet, in the counting dark, a dead house's daughter is holding her breath among the drowned.
dmlog.dmNotes: Deception gamble vs a wary Circle hunter, genuine-sanction lever = adv, DC15, Wren exposed below = real stakes. Success = hunter turned + proof in hand (lever obtained). NearMiss = he verifies the checkable part (walks her to the den — costs the night + a suspicion-tick), proof still got. Fail = he was briefed to watch for the well-house, her screening draws him to it — alliance+location BURNED, Wren trapped below, finale from a worse spot. No front tick (a hunter-encounter, not a faction clock move).

dmlog.text: He lets you finish, and then he doesn't ship the oars — he digs one into the mud and holds the boat exactly where it is. "See, they didn't just say you'd be up here," he says, mild as milk. "They said you'd be up here being useful about a bend, and to mind whether the use pointed at the well-house. And here's Corran's tired girl, doing all her walking between me and one particular door." He steps out onto the mud, unhurried, and starts up the bank PAST you toward the canted house — not running, never running, just going to look at the thing your whole body has been standing in front of — and below, the well's throat is a trap with a Sunn still in it and no way up that he won't see. Your cover didn't just fail; it drew him the last hundred yards to the one place it was built to hide.

dm.coverBurnedT7: T7-set09 (Deception FAIL): the hunter was briefed to watch whether Sella's 'use' pointed at the well-house — and her over-eager screening drew him straight to it. He walked PAST her up the bank toward the canted house while Wren was still in the well's throat. ALLIANCE + LOCATION EXPOSED to the Circle: Corran will now learn his suspected eyes were bodily guarding a specific upriver house. Sella is BURNED as a straight liar caught in the act; the finale opens from a much worse position (a Circle professional at the door, Wren trapped below, violence or flight the only outs). Live existential danger.

dm.descentTrapT7: T7-set09 (fail): Wren is in the well's throat retrieving the proof when the hunter breaks past Sella toward the house — she must surface into being seen, abort, or be trapped below. Proof possibly secured but the retrieval is compromised and the last Sunn is one bad moment from the exact fate her house spent a century avoiding.

dmlog.text: He's already decided I'm nothing, and that's the only weapon I've got left, so I don't argue and I don't draw — I fall in half a step behind his shoulder like a scolded creature trailing her better, still talking, still bored, "fine, fine, look all you like, there's a rotted hatch and a dead fire and I'll be the one explaining to Corran why his man fell through a hundred-year floor —" keeping my voice a whine so his ears stay on my mouth and not my hands. And I steer the walk. I know this ground; I read it in the last light. There's a pale cord strung ankle-high across the only dry approach, and just past it the glass-lip where the whole house drank itself drunk-deep, milk-green and slick and no footing at all. I walk him at it, chattering, unthreatening, matching his unhurried pace right up until his lead boot finds Wren's cord in the dark — and the instant he's caught mid-stride, off his line, I stop being the tired girl. Everything I've got goes into one shove, low and driving, the whole weight the last five days owe somebody, aimed to put a Circle professional off that slick lip and into the glass that keeps what it takes — because I drowned a man cleaner than this once for less, and this one came up the river to bury the last of a murdered house.

It works the way a thing works when a professional has already filed you under harmless — he lets you trail his shoulder, half-listening to the whine of Corran's tired girl, his eyes on the canted house and not on the woman he's decided is furniture. You walk him up the dark approach chattering, matching his unhurried pace, steering the line of it a foot at a time toward the pale glimmer of Wren's cord and the drunk glass-lip beyond, where the whole world goes slick and milk-green and lends no foot a grip. His lead boot finds the cord. For one instant the unhurried man is off his line, weight pitched forward into a stride the ground just stole — and in that instant you stop being furniture. Everything the last five days owe somebody goes down into your legs and out through both hands, low and driving, aimed to put a hundred-year killer off that lip and into the glass that keeps what it takes. The shove lands. Whether a man who has survived this long survives one more slick step is the only question left on the river.
dmlog.dmNotes: Athletics ambush-shove, terrain+underestimation lever = adv, DC15, lethal intent. Success = hunter into the glass (vanished, deferred Corran-cost) + Wren surfaces with the proof (lever secured). NearMiss = he twists to mud not glass, drags Sella into a knife-close grapple at the lip (hp -3), fight live into T9. Fail = a pro rides the cord/shove, takes her wrists, calls the house — Sella held, Wren surfacing into discovery, alliance blown. No front tick (a lone-hunter fight). No combat_start fired — a shove-scuffle resolves in fiction; keeps the finale on the Sunn reveal, not the initiative machinery.

dmlog.text: A man who has walked away from this work for twenty years has walked away by keeping his feet — and tonight, one time, the glass takes that from him. The cord holds his boot a half-beat too long; your whole driving weight arrives while his balance is already gone; and he goes off the lip backward with the particular silent surprise of the competent meeting the one thing they didn't check. No shout — there's no time for a shout. Just the slick green closing over an unhurried man, and the glass doing the thing the glass does, taking him down into the color with the counting dead, unhurried itself now, in no rush at all. The river runs on. His empty boat knocks against the mud. And behind you the floor-hatch scrapes and Wren comes up streaming and shaking with the amber-dark resin clutched to her chest — the deed, the name, the whole buried lie — into a night you have just bought her at the price of a second Circle man the Maw will never find. Corran will do that sum one day. Not tonight.

dm.secondManGoneT8: T8-set09 (Athletics success, adv): after her cover crit-burned, Sella put the inbound Circle hunter off the canted glass-lip (using Wren's ankle-cord + his underestimation of 'Corran's tired girl') into the glass — a clean vanish, no wound, the crater keeps what it takes (mirrors her clerk-drowning T5-set05). SECOND Circle man to disappear upriver in her vicinity (after Ossle/Vesk in set-05). Corran gets no report back from this hunter — a silence a patient man will eventually price. Not tonight; a deferred, mounting exposure. Sella committed further to the necessary-killing path.

dm.proofSecuredT8: T8-set09: Wren surfaced from the glass with the LEVER — the true deed of the Throat + the roll of the Sunns' suppressed true name, in rot-proof resin — the moment Sella ended the hunter. Proof IS IN HAND; the alliance survived its first shared kill/crisis. The plan (name loud at the Tree-courthouse) is armed and the immediate threat cleared, at the cost of a vanished Circle man.

dmlog.text: I get Wren up out of the shallows and back to her careful fire, and I let neither of us look too long at the empty boat knocking the mud — that's a weight for a quieter night. "Dry it off. Show me," I say, gentle now the killing's done. "Not to steal it. To aim it. You want your name said loud enough it can't be un-said — then I need to know every word this thing gives me, because a lever you don't understand is a lever that breaks in your hand." And I read it the way I read the parcel that started all this, five days and a lifetime ago — the professional's slow eye, the resin peeled along its own grain, the deed of the Throat and the roll of the Sunn name laid out in the firelight. I read WHOSE hand signed the well away, whose mark witnessed the giving, what house held the door open from the inside — and I lay it against everything I've been carrying and never spent: a chandler's hidden floorboard, a netmender's secret I've kept like a coin in my cheek, an Iron-Strap guild that has wanted its "lost homeland" back the whole time I've been in this town. I want the name the Traitor's Tree wouldn't give me. And I have a cold feeling I've been holding a piece of it in my own pocket since Day Two.

Wren dries the resin at the fire and cracks it along its grain the way you showed her, and the hundred years come out into the light: the deed of the Throat, real, sealed, a well given freely — not taken, GIVEN, the word right there in the old formal hand, which is the whole difference between a conquest a town forgets and a crime a town could still be made to feel. And under the granting-hand, the witness-mark. You know it before your mind will let you say you know it, because you have been carrying its twin folded in your cheek since Day Two: the iron strap, the little bound-buckle sigil, the mark of the house that has spent every day you've been in this town whining about a lost homeland it wants restored.

The Iron-Strap. It was never the Circle who opened the Sunn door. It was the Strap — the hand that ate at the table, that signed the well across and let the Circle be the ones to hold the knife — and then spent a hundred years poor and bitter and 'wronged,' wanting back the very thing they SOLD. Maddan. The netmender, the secret you kept like a coin, the floorboard under Rell's chandlery — all of it the same rotten timber, all of it the Strap keeping its own guilty deed buried right alongside the Sunns they buried it with. You came up this river for a lever against the man who owns you, and you have pulled a floorboard up on your OWN guild — the criminal house you're tied to in this town — and found the founding murder under it.

And then you read the roll of the name, and you go very quiet. Wren watches your face do the thing faces do. "You've got it," she says, not a question. You have. The true name of the last Sunn, the small suppressed thing a hundred years of patient men killed to keep quiet, is sitting in your head now in the firelight — and you do not say it aloud, not here, not to the reeds, because a name like that gets spent ONCE and you will not waste it on the dark. "I've got it," you tell her. "And Wren — it's worse and better than you know. The hand that opened your door is still in this town, still bitter, still reachable. Your name can bury Corran. But the same breath that says it names the traitors too — and one of them is a man I've got a knife on already." You have the whole lever now, both edges of it, and the only question left in the Maw is where a woman with all the time in the world decides to swing it.

dm.deedReadT9: T9-set09: Sella + Wren cracked the resin and read the lever together. The deed reads the well was GIVEN (freely granted, not conquered — the word is in the formal hand) = the traitor's-gift the whole plan rests on. Sella now KNOWS Wren's true suppressed Sunn name (read off the roll) — deliberately UNSPOKEN in fiction (saved to be said ONCE, loud, at the Tree; recorded dm-only for continuity as 'Ilsa Sunn'). The full lever is in hand: the name buries Corran's claim, but naming it also exposes the traitor-house.

dm.foundingTraitorSolvedT9: T9-set09 EARNED CONVERGENCE (no roll — the payoff of accumulated state the pressured Tree-read T8-set4 lacked): the deed's WITNESS/granting mark is the Iron-Strap sigil. Sella solved it by laying the deed against the secret she's carried since Day 2 (Maddan's Iron-Strap secret, unspent), Rell's hidden floorboard, and the Iron-Strap 'restore a lost homeland' agenda. THE FOUNDING BETRAYAL WAS THE IRON-STRAP LINE'S — they opened the Sunn door / signed the well across to the Circle ('the hand that ate at the table'), then spent a century poor and bitter wanting back what they SOLD. Maddan Strole = the living keeper of that guilty deed. Aligns with the DM-truth ('the door was Maddan's own betrayal'). Sella's unspent Maddan-secret is now understood as a piece of the founding crime.

dm.traitorHouseRevealedT9: T9-set09: revealed (via the deed) as the FOUNDING TRAITOR-HOUSE — the Iron-Strap gave/signed the Sunns' well to the Ironwood Circle a hundred years ago, then recast themselves as the 'wronged' house wanting a 'lost homeland/status' restored (their agenda). COMPLICATION: Sella herself is tied to the Iron-Strap (her Day-1 criminal origin-tie), so her lever against Corran also detonates her own guild + Maddan (whom she has a knife on). The long-dormant Iron-Strap (2/6) is now central and double-edged — swinging the lever cuts three houses at once (Circle, Iron-Strap, and Sella's own footing).

payload.rel: opened the Sunn door / signed away the Throat (founding betrayal)

dmlog.dmNotes: Earned convergence, no roll — the deed she physically holds + a secret she's carried since Day 2 + safety = the traitor-solve the pressured Tree-read (T8-set4) couldn't give. The founding traitor-house = the Iron-Strap (Maddan the living keeper), consistent with DM-truth; complication = it's Sella's OWN guild-tie, so the lever is triple-edged. Wren's true name READ but held UNSPOKEN (saved for T10's loud moment; recorded dm-only). Poised the close on the choice: how/whether to swing a lever that cuts Corran, the Iron-Strap, AND Sella's own footing.

dmlog.text: "Here's where I don't swing it," I tell her, and I watch that land wrong before I fix it. "Not because I won't. Because a name spent tonight is a name spent cheap — two dead women and a drowned Circle man shouting into a reed-bed, and by noon Corran's called it grief-madness and salted the ground where we stood. You waited a hundred years to be said out loud, Wren. Give me a handful more days to build the room where it can't be un-said." I lay it out plain, the long game, the only kind I've ever won. "Your proof goes back in the glass where only you can reach it — I carry the KNOWING, not the paper; a paper can be taken off my corpse, a thing in my head can't. You move your bed; that near-shutter trick saved you tonight but a man came right to it, so it's burned. And I go back down that river the good, tired, diligent creature, with a true report about a sluice-gate and a wrecker-den, and one dead man I'll never mention — and I hold your name under my tongue like the knife it is. When I say it, it'll be at his tree, in front of his town, on a day I've stacked so high he can't patient his way out of it. You have my word, and you're holding my grave, so my word's worth something for once." And then I do the thing I do at the end of every one of these long nights: I take the ledger of it, honest. I came up this river for a lever and I found the whole lie the Maw is built on. I made an ally of a ghost and a corpse of a hunter. I've got the man who owns me by a throat he doesn't know I can reach — and the man I've had a knife on for a week just turned out to be a founding traitor. Fine, Corran. You said you'd work the sum of me. I've been working yours right back, and tonight it finally came out whole. I turn my face downriver, and I start walking home to my leash — carrying the one thing in the Maw that can cut it.

Wren hears you out, and the anger you braced for doesn't come — because she is, under the hunted animal, a strategist too, and she knows the sound of the only plan that ends with her alive AND said. "A handful of days," she repeats, and there's a century of waiting in how lightly she manages to hold the words. "I've got practice." She takes the resin back and she'll sink it again where only a Sunn goes, and she'll move her bed, and the near-shutter trick will get retired the way all a survivor's best tricks eventually do. Then she does the thing that seals it, the only currency two dead women trade in: she tells you the name. The real one. Out loud, once, quiet, to you and the fire and the counting glass — not the spending of it, just the trusting of it, handing you the loaded thing and letting you see she knows you could fire it at her instead of for her. "Now you're not holding my name," she says. "You're holding ME. Same as I'm holding your grave. Go be diligent, coat. Come back loud."

And so the long night closes the way your long nights do — not with a blow struck but with a knife banked, honed, and hidden under the tongue. You turn your face downriver. Behind you a well-house settles a little deeper into the glass that keeps what it takes, one drowned Circle man heavier than it was at dusk, and the last Sunn goes back to her patient dark to wait out a handful more days after a hundred years. Ahead of you the chains of the Maw catch the first grey of Day Six, and somewhere under them a patient man is waiting for his tired creature to come back with a true report about a sluice-gate, never dreaming she's bringing home the one sum he can't work: that the well he rules by is a gift a traitor made, that the traitor's own guilty house is the one Sella Voss is tied to, and that the name to unmake all of it is sitting under her tongue like a coin she has finally, after a lifetime of spending everyone else's, decided to save. You walk home to your leash, Voss. You just don't tell it you've been sharpening the thing that cuts it. He said he'd work the sum of you. Let him. The answer's in your mouth now, and you get to choose the morning you say it out loud.

payload.what: The Shimmering Maw's burning-water well was a traitor's GIFT, not a conquest — the Ironwood Circle's whole claim to the Throat rests on a betrayal, and the last of the murdered Sunns still lives upriver, holding the proof that could unmake it.

dm.pactSealedT10: T10-set09 CLOSE: alliance sealed into real trust — Wren spoke her TRUE suppressed name aloud to Sella (recorded dm-only 'Ilsa Sunn'), not to spend it but to TRUST it ('now you're holding ME, same as I'm holding your grave'). Pact: Sella will make the name loud at the Traitor's-Tree courthouse before the whole town, but on HER timing — 'a handful of days' to stack the room so Corran can't patient his way out of it (not tonight = a name spent cheap). Wren re-sinks the proof in the glass (only-a-Sunn lock), moves her bed (the near-shutter trick burned). Sella carries the KNOWING (name + traitor-solve), NOT the paper (a paper comes off a corpse; a thing in the head doesn't). Provisional ally → committed ally, mutual-hostage-and-now-mutual-faith.

dm.setCloseState09: T10-set09 CLOSE (Day 6 dawn): Sella turns downriver to return as Corran's diligent creature with a TRUE errand-report (flood-source sluice-gate + wrecker-den) and one dead hunter she'll never mention — leash INTACT, cover rebuilt on true coin. She now secretly holds the ULTIMATE lever: the Circle's Throat-claim is a traitor's gift, the last Sunn lives with proof, and Sella holds the true name to say it loud at his own Tree. She BANKED it (patient long-game, mirrors her set-07 close) rather than spending it cheap. Undissolved: Corran's T6-set4 interest in her. Mounting deferred sum: a SECOND vanished Circle man upriver (after Ossle/Vesk). Sella's four-secrets ledger: spent the 'drowned-hero' to Wren (T5); gained TWO new cards (Wren's name + the Iron-Strap/Maddan founding-traitor solve). Triple-edged: swinging the lever also burns her own Iron-Strap tie + Maddan.

dmlog.dmNotes: Close honors the patient choice — no premature loud reveal (banked, not spent; mirrors set-07's 'a knife doesn't have to be drawn to be a knife'). Pact sealed (Wren trusts Sella with the true name; proof re-hidden; Wren relocates). fact_canonized = a durable Sella-KNOWN world truth (not a dmOnly dump — she solved it) → should grant legit +1 XP (BUG-15 clear check). New equilibrium: leashed + diligent-cover-rebuilt, holding the ultimate triple-edged lever unspent, a mounting deferred second-dead-man cost, a committed Sunn ally upriver. Set closes tenser AND richer.
